analysis.title: "Higher Ground": Rabobank Says The Fed Pushed The 10Y To 5%... Then The Debt Took Over
key_insights: Rabobank (Philip Marey, US Special 'Higher Ground') splits the 2026 rise in the 10Y into two selloffs: the move to 5% reflected the Fed shifting from thinking about cuts to hiking in September, and the move well above 5% reflected a rise in the term premium driven by concerns about public debt.
Using the NY Fed ACM model, the risk-neutral yield rose steadily from the Feb 28 start of the Iran war while the term premium went essentially nowhere for most of 2026.

In the first three weeks of September the 10Y rose from 4.80% to 4.96%, the term premium fell from 0.78% to 0.57%, and the risk-neutral yield rose from 4.09% to 4.43%. The FOMC hiked 25bps that month and signaled another hike in the dot plot.

After Sept 23 the term premium rose from 0.57% to 0.98% by Oct 7 while the risk-neutral yield fell from 4.43% to 4.39%. Rabobank says the bond market shifted from worrying about the Fed to worrying about the borrower.

Rabobank links the term premium turn to the MOVE index, which jumped from 78.6 on Sept 22 to 95.5 on Sept 23, and names the weak 5-year Treasury auction that day as the likely main cause. The $70B 5Y sale priced at 5.033%, the first 5%+ yield since 2007, tailed by 3.1bps, with Indirects at the lowest since March 2020 and dealers holding 15.8%.

TIPS decomposition: the real 10Y yield rose from 2.44% (Sept 1) to 2.63% (Sept 22) and 2.95% (Oct 5), while breakevens moved only 2.35% to 2.33% to 2.36%. Rabobank says energy prices from the war and a resilient US economy raised the real policy rate path, and the Fed's hawkish reaction kept inflation expectations anchored.

Goldman (William Marshall, 'The Factors Behind the Rise in US Yields') says the 10Y is up 130bps since the eve of the Iran war, and about 70% of the move in longer-term forwards reflects hawkish Fed repricing. Consensus 1y-ahead short-rate forecasts rose about 125bp, worth about 55bp to longer-term forwards. About 10-15bp of the year-to-date move is unexplained by fundamentals.

Goldman agrees the latest leg was a long-end move but attributes the term premium rise mostly to higher macro uncertainty and Treasuries no longer hedging equities (yields rise with oil, stocks fall when yields rise), not to the fiscal outlook. Marshall says the fiscal trajectory is unsustainable but has not meaningfully shifted, and finds little evidence that AI-related debt supply has an outsized or durable effect on yields.

Rabobank expects the 10Y to stay above 4.30%, the level seen in the six months before the war (now about 1 percentage point higher), because the AI boom supports the economy and limits downside from a revision of Fed expectations. It expects the term premium to trend upward because it sees no progress on public debt.

Rabobank forecasts a second Fed hike in December, the 10Y sideways at 5.20% through year-end, then 5.10% by mid-2027 and 5.00% by end-2027 with inflation slowing to 2.2% and cuts in 2028. Markets price 3-4 more hikes, which Rabobank views as overdone.

Goldman recommends establishing a foothold in duration: 5y5y yields at 5.5-5.6% are 40-50bps above fair value (about one standard deviation cheap), and its bond fund duration indicator is at -2, a level historically followed by lower yields over 3-6 months.

Goldman estimates MBS negative convexity forced about $60B of 10Y-equivalent selling since the start of September (likely on the high side of realized flows), plus $10-15B from cheapest-to-deliver switches in futures. MBS convexity is now about zero, so that amplifier is mostly spent. Higher yields would lift the financial conditions drag on growth from 0.2pp to more than 0.5pp.

Goldman's year-end 10Y target is 4.75%, versus Rabobank's 5.20%. Goldman sees upside risks if energy risks remain unresolved and growth risks stay low, and says a credible reduction in energy risks, weaker growth news or diminished confidence in the AI trade would take yields sharply lower.

Market snapshot Oct 13-14: the 10Y fell as much as 6bps to 5.18% after the Columbus Day holiday as oil fell and traders trimmed hike bets, with swaps implying three more hikes. The 10Y briefly hit 5.36% last week, the highest since 2002. Apollo's Slok found the same two drivers in the D'Amico-Kim-Wei model. The IMF's Vamvakidis called surging government bond yields the biggest emerging risk to the global financial system.

The author sides with Rabobank, arguing positioning, valuation and technicals can produce a rally but do not address the deficit, absent central bank buyers or hyperscaler issuance competing for long-end demand. Citi expects the Treasury to sell fewer long bonds and more bills.

risk_factors: Further ugly Treasury auctions, with the author noting the next one is never more than a week away.
A marginal core CPI beat could be problematic for rates (Goldman mortgage desk).
Public debt trajectory, lack of central bank demand and hyperscaler debt issuance competing for long-end demand (Citi: 'partly cannibalizing').
10Y moving toward 5.50%, which JPM calls anathema for stocks.
Energy risks remaining unresolved and Fed neutral rate revisions upward.
IMF's Vamvakidis: surging government bond yields are the biggest emerging risk to the global financial system.
vol_and_positioning: MOVE index rose from 78.6 to 95.5 on Sept 23 and has tracked the term premium since.
Goldman's bond fund duration indicator is at -2, an underweight that has historically preceded lower yields over the next 3-6 months.
Goldman's 1y10y swaption vol is the volatility gauge it pairs with its own term premium estimate.
The author notes the VIX stayed calm during the rates vol episode as it spilled into credit.
Goldman estimates MBS negative convexity forced about $60B of 10Y-equivalent selling since the start of September, with index MBS convexity now about zero.
geopolitical: War with Iran began Feb 28, with Hormuz disruptions raising oil, gasoline and diesel prices and pushing the Fed from cut expectations to hikes.
Rabobank links the grinding rise in term premium partly to an unstable geopolitical climate and lack of central bank demand.
The author cites Japan repatriating funds and France 'going full PIIGS' as additional supports for a higher term premium.
cross_bank_references: Rabobank attributes the move above 5% to public debt; Goldman attributes the term premium mostly to macro uncertainty and Treasuries failing to hedge equities, finding little evidence that AI debt supply matters.
Citi warned hyperscaler issuance may be 'partly cannibalizing' long-end Treasury demand.
Citi expects Washington to sell fewer long bonds and more bills.
JPM (Feroli) core CPI at 0.18% vs Goldman 0.24%.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman: 5y5y is 40-50bps above fair value, bond fund duration is at -2, MBS convexity selling is mostly spent, and higher yields drag growth and widen credit spreads, so a brake on further selloffs. Year-end 10Y target 4.75%.
tension_points.bear_case: Rabobank: the public debt is not fading and the term premium trends upward, so even if Fed hike expectations fade the downside to yields is limited. 10Y sideways at 5.20% through year-end.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Goldman's call fails if energy risks stay unresolved and growth risks stay low. A credible reduction in energy risks, weaker growth news or diminished confidence in the AI trade would take yields sharply lower.

theme_stances.key_argument: The most recent peak in the term premium was related to public debt, and no progress is expected, so it is likely to remain trending upward.
theme_stances.evidence: public debt is not fading. In fact, it could become the most persistent driver

theme_stances.key_argument: Cheap valuation, underweight positioning and spent technicals argue for establishing a foothold in duration.
Downside potential from a revision of monetary policy expectations is limited because the AI boom could support the economy beyond this year.
theme_stances.evidence: the AI boom could support the economy well beyond this year
